title: Thai Basil Chicken

ingredientGroups.title: Chicken
items: 1.5-2 lbs boneless/skinless chicken thigh, medium-fine mince/ground

ingredientGroups.title: Vegetables
items: 1 cup green beans, cut into 1” segments (chinese long bean)

ingredientGroups.title: Garlic and Chiles
items: 4 Birds Eye chili peppers, stems removed
2 Tbsp mild red peppers, minced (bell pepper is fine)

ingredientGroups.title: For Stir-Frying
items: 2 cups Holy Basil leaves (or Thai Basil), washed and drained

steps: In a medium bowl, combine the chicken, cornstarch, white pepper, and oil until distributed.

Using a mortar and pestle, crush the chili peppers until it reaches a fine consistency.  Add the garlic and mild peppers and continue to crush the mixture until combined.  The goal is to break up the chilis so there are no spicy chunks but not ground to a paste.  Transfer to a small bowl and set aside.
In a small bowl, combine the oyster sauce, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar, and water.

Arrange all your ingredients so they are nearby and ready to use prior to stir-frying.  The following steps happen in rapid sequence and can burn if the next set of ingredients are not ready or easily accessible.
Heat a wok until smoking, then turn the heat down to medium and add 2-3 Tbsp of oil.  Immediately add the garlic chili mixture and fry, moving the mixture quickly to avoid burning the garlic.
When the chilis are fragrant, add the meat and turn the heat up to medium-high.  Keep the mixture moving quickly to avoid burnt garlic or chicken.
Add the veggies after the chicken releases its moisture, approximately 30-45 seconds.  Continue to stir fry until the beans reach the desired doneness, approximately 30-45 seconds.
Add the sauce, tossing for 15 seconds to combine. Before removing from the heat, check that the chicken has reached 165°F.
Finally, turn off the heat and add the basil, tossing to combine.  The basil will wilt from the residual heat.
Serve immediately with rice and optionally top with a crispy fried egg.
